In short, this game has AMAZING ART STYLE but its gameplay leave a lot to be desired. It is not a BAD GAME, but it's not a GOOD GAME either, at the current state it's an 'OKAY GAME'. If you are interested in the game, I suggest waiting until more major updates drop OR wait until it leaves EA (which might take a while). Pros: -THE ART! IT'S AMAZING! -Punkz (Imo, the best) Cons: -Gameplay -Lack of strategical depth (Like having no Zone of Control) -Map buildings in boss stage (Just in this stage, other stages are fine) -Unit balance -No campaign (as of the writing of this review) ANIWARS is a roguelite-grid-turnbased squad game where your anime waifus squad of maximum six fought against other waifu squads of random sizes in a roguelite zones map. The game is very simple, too simple and lacking in substance in my opinion, that it make units that can move the furthest King, and units that can PUSH other units Queen--why? Because the maps have 'hazard zones' that if a unit were pushed there they INSTANTLY DIED, no question ask. On the surface this is no problem, in fact it expand on the strategical depth of the game, but the game have one critical problem: It has no Zone of Control (ZoC). This lets units moves past enemies units and caused havoc to the backline, or pushers to push units out of bound really easily. It made playing as the more rigid and formation based faction, like the SOLDIERS (or whatever they're called) really annoying, especially if you haven't unlock their tank units. The AI are build around this, so they'll be hunting your backline like sharks and there's very little you can do to stop it. This also revealed another problem; the factions. Amazing art style and thematic aside, I've played and finished 2 out of the 3 currently available faction, the SOLDIERS (Blitz?) and PUNKZ (The best), and I've enjoyed playing the later more because they are an aggressive, mostly high mobility factions. With no ZoC, my bike units caused chaos and just run around the map capturing buildings and targeting the AI squishy units while my slower but high damage cleavers march slowly to the frontline like the rumbling. But when I go back to the slower soldier faction it became miserable and annoying again, especially if you're fighting against PUNKZ. They also have other unique things like neutral buildings that, if captured, give you minor boons or even let you damage units. This is okay, until you reached the Boss Zone. Not only does the enemy have an extra unit more than you, they have most of the buildings on their side, most of them are annoying to deal with like giving the AI stupid level of buffs and/or heals them, even one where it'll keep giving them stronger buffs per turn the longer you leave it alone. It's not fun anymore, it became annoying to play. I know it's the boss zone, but is it necessary to make it THAT annoying? Ranting aside, I think this game has potential but I can't in good conscious recommend it at its current form. Not even PUNKZ, my beloveds, can change my mind (yet). I hope the best of luck to the devs!

There's a solid underlayer here overlaid with balancing decisions that are at best decently challenging and at worst, outright unfairly loaded in the AI's favor. I think my breaking point was when I reached the boss stage on the same round it spawned (so no buffs for them) and the enemy troops that had formerly been hitting my units for a modest 20-60 damage on average were suddenly hitting them for almost their entire health bar with a single attack. I couldn't itemize my way around this absurd power spike like the game expects me to with items being the only way to beef up your units between stages because I didn't know what I was getting into nor would I have been likely to have gotten the items I needed from previous stages to build around this power spike. That aside, while the idea of an SRPG/Advance-wars-like roguelike is novel, the tactical depth on the strategy side leaves one wanting. There is no 'zone of control' around units, there is no pre-battle map showcase, a lot of the time enemies spawn with several buildings providing buffs on their side of the map which can be very difficult to reach (makes sense they need something since they don't get items like the player but I swear they get a stacking invisible buff to their stats the further you progress through a run). Your unit's value are measured soley in what items they carry since there isn't a veterancy or level system, so keeping your starting roster alive for the whole run or winning a hard-fought fight after a bad battle to get back on your feet where your more outnumbered than usual can end up ringing a bit hollow. At least in my opinion. Despite my torrent of negativity, I do think with some spit polish and shine this game can shape out to be a very good strategy roguelike with an excellent artstyle to boot, but with the current state of balance... I guess if you like unexpected kicks to the stomach after smooth sailing for 40-minute's work?

TL;DR: GOTY. The game hooked me in with the art, but I stayed for the gameplay. The art is fantastic, don't get me wrong: every character, every item are made really well, and are delightful in different ways, though Rocket and Big Kitty will always be my favorites. The gameplay is what makes it the best game ever, though, as it is always challenging, and took me quite some time to stop losing again, and again, and again. I cleared a few fights here and there, gathered some items, but still lost against the boss in the end of the runs again, and again, and again. Every run has been lots of fun, I was losing because I was making mistakes and misjudging situations, and it was up to me to fix it. 36 hours in, I have a few builds I like to run for my units, a few presets I favor, some items and general strategies I like, and nowadays I do not struggle as much, finishing more runs than I fail, though I still have trouble with keeping my squishies alive, and the amount of yeet's I've experienced is illegal. The random element makes runs unique, as surely it's best if I get the BiS for my Akimbo, but what if I don't? Shifting compositions around unit items and commander items is rewarding, though sometimes it drives me insane to get the bad RNG. Game's not perfect. It's not finished (it is in early access for a reason): there are still commanders to be released, higher difficulty setting, more things to do. There are mechanical inconsistensies like Merc Hood's effect doesn't stack unlike pretty much every other item in the game, or that Akimbo's Bunny Hop doesn't get counted as tiles traveled, but those tiny issues are so minor in comparison to how fun and enjoyable everything in this game is, how infuratingly simple and silly some of the battles are, and I can't wait to see what updates devs will put out. There is lore, there are stories, there are quirks to commanders, but I can't say much about that, besides that Nova is my favorite commander, and Hydra is my most successful one. I struggle the most with Blitz, though I don't think she's as weak as I initially thought. There are challenges that unlock gear for future runs, and some of those challenges are either difficult to accomplish, or you need to be clairvoyant, as they are secret (I'm sure there's a guide already somewhere), and I got all but one of them on my own by just playing and not paying that much attention. I wish there was more content: more arenas to fight in, more bioms, more synergies and more events, but the game does get updates, and I'm happy to wait.

Love the game honestly, probably my favorite of the genre, the reliance on making builds and getting passives over the course of the run feels great and quite unique and the amount of things you can unlock has made even version .2 feel nearly fully fleshed out. However, yes, the game is very difficult but I see it as a heavy learning curve which I love, the AI actually strategizes to move your unit into a spot so that the next can insta kill it through knock back and that means you have to look out for more then just the immediate threat and that is not something you get often making wins feel very earned. From recent patch notes I have noticed a pretty big decrease in difficulty and a nerfing to fun items and I must request to keep the spirit of those items alive, while yes punkzerker paint led to a breacher being able to 1v6 and win with the proper build that exact situation is what makes the game so wacky and fun and I would really like to see it keep its personality so I beg of you to reconsider these choices. Overall, I do recommend the game even now at full price because frankly 12$ is more then worth it and I eagerly await the games development.

Do you like advance wars? Do you like waifus? Well have I got the game for you! Aniwars is a fun little rogue lite spin on the advance wars formula. Instead of of large scale conflicts, you're typically managing smaller skirmishes; with a max squad size of six, and a wide array of units and items to keep each encounter feeling unique and fresh. That said, the game is still early in development. It doesn't take long to figure out what items you want to go for with each unit, and what unit combinations provide the most consistent reward vs. risk factor. Still, the road to getting to that point is pretty fun. And I don't regret my time with it at all. As you can see based on the thumbs up, I recommend the game, even in its current state, however with some caveats. If the idea of a slightly more basic advance wars with anime waifus doesn't appeal to you, then I don't think the game really provides much in its current state to warrant purchasing at this time. Even then, fans of the genre might find the current experience to be quite shallow. So why recommend it? Well, the past few patches have not only demonstrated to me a commitment to adding content to the game, but also a willingness to listen and adapt to player feedback. Patch 0.2.2 (the latest patch as of writing) addressed virtually all of my complaints from a balance perspective, laying a solid foundation for future content updates to come. I'm genuinely looking forward to what the developers have planned for the future, and I feel that well earned optimism warrants a recommendation.

As of current (0.2.2) patch I can recommend the game. It's got enough content to justify the (current) price and the foundation is there for a solid game. The gameplay is simple yet has some depth. If you're familiar with Advanced Wars and it's ilk, there's nothing surprising here. Unlike AW, the units here have no inherent weaknesses to each other. The directional damage is a nice addition and being able to push units off the battlefield is either frustrating or genious, depending if you're on the receiving end or not. Though it would be nice to be able to rotate your units in place or choose the direction they end up facing after completing their move. If not for tactical benefits then at least to help my built-like-a-brickhouse Breacher named Mastiffa hold a mountain pass while a Sniper with (dangerously delicious) amounts of lower body mAss 360-no-scopes over the aforementioned mountains. The art style is clean, crisp, consistent and character desing is varied and well-made. They were a big selling point for me and I can say I'm not disappointed. There are many games that plaster anime babes all over themselves to make up for lacking gameplay or mechanics but here it isn't the case. Personally I didn't find the difficulty to be too egregious. Bosses do have bit of a spike but ever since the latest changes to them, they are very manageable. RNG of course plays a role here and considering what items and units you get, the bosses CAN wipe the floor with you. But having said that, I found this games RNG to be much more forgiving compared to some other roguelikes. In most of my runs I didn't feel like I was getting shafted out of good items or were denied an unit I needed. The story is there but it's limited. It's mainly told via item descriptions and small amounts of dialogue between the Commanders. It's not a bad thing in itself as it keeps the attention on the gameplay (and the girls) but if you're looking for a strategy game with emphasis to story, look elsewhere. But I must say I did find myself intrigued just why these borderline hentai heroines are beating the living daylights out of each other so here's hoping that gets expanded upon. If I had to give some criticism, my main complaint as of now is the limited amount of units (and maybe maps). You quickly see them all and it makes multiple runs feel somewhat samey. If and when the devs add more of them, I think this game is in a very good place. In summary: 9/10, needs more hot women.

Great Strategy Game as someone who DOESNT play strategy games I've followed the artist for sometime prior to the game's release, after generously being given a free copy of the game by a friend I gave it a shot! I am BAD at these games which is why they don't get long playtime out of me, however Aniwars kept me hooked with its great art style and character designs and its simple but not easy gameplay. The added roguelike elements with more items to use in game from completing challenges related to the units, allowing you to have more experience with them and to better understand how they function for future runs. These allow for constant replayability rather than just completing the game off a single successful run. Any bugs that have been reported to the small hard working team are patched out very quickly with plenty of updates and new commanders/units coming soon that I'm excited for. I've had hours into this game already and I still think about the itch to play another run from time to time, excellent gem more people should give a shot!

I’ve played around 32.8 hours, and I honestly had a great time with it. The customization for units is one of my favorite parts of the game. Being able to experiment with different setups and playstyles makes every run feel fresh and gives you a lot of freedom in how you approach battles. The art style is also fantastic and gives the game a really lively and energetic atmosphere. I also enjoyed the campaign, even though it’s fairly short. The amount of choices you can make throughout the game keeps the gameplay interesting and adds replay value. There’s a lot of variety depending on how you want to build and play. My favorite commander is Blitz by far. If you enjoy strategy games with solid customization, charming visuals, and meaningful gameplay choices, I’d definitely recommend giving this game a try.

I like the concept, the art style, the ideas. HOWEVER, the execution, especially when it comes to balancing, is a pain in the a**. There are units that are too good (breachers), and others are too garbage (rockets); plus the constant scaling of the enemy factions versus whatever trash item you can mob up makes it less of a learning curve but a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 90 degrees cliff with blades sticking out of it after the second map is cleared. The maps themselves are problematic, what is the point of having a faction that rely on constantly moving around when 3/4 of the maps are chokepoints; and the AI will one hundred percent having control of said chokepoints before you can? I really love the game, and I know it is still in Early Access, so I have high hope that the bouncing issue that is balancing can be adjusted accordingly.

(just don't be a stingy commander) There's also items which can really buff your squad but the game wouldn't turn into cake walk since enemies can get their own buildings to survive against your items & consumables. Your Eliminated Units will bring their items to the grave (so don't be a stingy commander) I don't understand why some review says it was unfair for enemies getting building buffs when you can still one shot them with a decent unit build, or tank attacks from them. Overall in this early stage? it's a good game.
